Chapter 6: Stepping Into Leadership—Finding Her Voice.
Have you ever noticed how sometimes, life seems to hold its breath, just waiting for you to make a move? For her, that moment arrived quietly. There was no spotlight, no big announcement—just this gentle but persistent feeling that she couldn’t stay silent any longer. All those years of struggle, all the mistakes and the hard-won resilience—they’d given her something powerful: a voice people actually wanted to hear.
It didn’t start with a big speech, either. At work, she began to speak up in meetings, finally sharing ideas she’d kept tucked away. The first time, her hands shook under the table—but she spoke anyway. And you know what? A few colleagues nodded. That tiny bit of support gave her the courage to keep going. Soon, she was volunteering for projects no one else wanted, taking on roles that stretched her in ways she hadn’t expected. Each risk, each new challenge, helped her see just how much she was capable of.
Outside the office, life pulled her into something new. A neighbor asked for help organizing a local event, and before she knew it, she was leading a team of volunteers. The work was tough—but it meant something. She started to notice how her story connected with others. By opening up about her own struggles and victories, she gave people around her permission to hope for themselves.
Of course, it wasn’t all smooth sailing. Not everyone was thrilled to see her step up. Some doubted she was up to the task. Others bristled at her ambition. But by now, she knew to expect resistance. Instead of backing down, she leaned into the discomfort. Criticism? She used it as fuel to get even stronger. She realized leadership wasn’t about having all the answers. It was about showing up, listening, and making room for other people to shine, too.
One night, after a long day filled with meetings and endless phone calls, she found herself alone in her little apartment, just thinking. The doubts still whispered, but they didn’t have the same hold on her anymore. She saw something clearly—most people wait for someone else to give them permission to lead. But really, the only permission that counts is the one you give yourself.
Leadership, she discovered, isn’t about titles or job descriptions. It’s about impact. It’s about lifting others as you climb—using your voice to open doors for those coming after you. Her journey was still unfolding, and there would be more challenges ahead. But she wasn’t waiting on the sidelines anymore. She’d found her voice. And with it, a new sense of purpose that felt bigger than anything she’d ever imagined.
